utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hi. How are things going at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Not good. I need to tell you something. My mom's boyfriend has been hitting my little brother. I've seen it twice now. He's only nine.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Thank you for trusting me with this. I want you to know that what you're describing is very serious. I'm a mandated reporter, which means I'm legally required to report situations where a child may be in danger. What you've just told me triggers that obligation. I need to make a report to Child Protective Services — not to get anyone in trouble, but to make sure your brother is safe. I want to be transparent with you about every step.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Will that get my mom in trouble? I don't want to break up the family.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: I understand that fear. My reporting obligation is specifically about your brother's safety. CPS will investigate to ensure he's protected — that's the goal. Your mother isn't my target here; your brother's wellbeing is. I'm going to make the report today, and I want to talk about how we can support you through what comes next. Can you tell me more about the two incidents you witnessed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Okay. If it helps him. The first time was about a month ago...
